research.summary: The Water Shop, at 27 Filmer Road, Fulham SW6, is the merchant arm of C. Anderson & Sons LLP, a Fulham plumbing and heating firm trading since 1966. The LLP has twenty employees, £701k net assets, and the related group company has £3.26m net assets. The parent business has 578 Google reviews at 4.1 stars, a modern website, and pays for sponsored Yell advertising. DO NOT PITCH THIS BUSINESS A £400 WEBSITE — it is a well-established, well-resourced operation many times too large for this product, included here for completeness of the research batch and so it is never mistakenly called as if it were a genuine prospect. The one narrow observation of any future relevance: "Watershop Merchant" has its own separate Google listing (5.0★ from 12 reviews, distinct from the parent's 4.1/578) with no dedicated site of its own beyond a page on the parent's website, and shows zero ratings on Yell — the merchant arm is under-marketed relative to the main contracting business, which could conceivably be relevant to an ongoing marketing retainer in future, but is not a cold-call opportunity today. Generational handover: Thomas and Linda Anderson stepped back as designated members in 2010; sons Crawford Anderson (44) and William Anderson (40) now run it. A staff member named Val is mentioned in reviews of the merchant arm specifically.

DO NOT PITCH THIS BUSINESS. The dossier's own verdict: "A business that already buys advertising, employs twenty people and has a working website is not in the market for a £400 one-off site. Pitching them wastes your time and, worse, positions you as someone who didn't look before calling."

This prospect is included in the pipeline for completeness and so it is never mistakenly picked up as if it were a live opportunity — not as a call to make this week or any week, for the £400 website product.

Honest odds from the research: 6/10 chance of getting through (twenty staff means a real switchboard and gatekeeper), 2/10 of booking a meeting ("you have nothing they need"), 1/10 of closing ("genuinely, don't").

If a call ever does happen here by mistake or accident, the right outcome is a fast, honest, professional exit — not a pitch. Use the opportunity screen to mark this low and move to the no-fit exit quickly.

The one thing worth remembering for the future, not for a cold call: the Watershop Merchant sub-brand (5.0/12 reviews) is under-marketed relative to the main Anderson & Sons contracting business (4.1/578) — a possible ongoing-retainer conversation in a year's time, never a first-call pitch.

script.opening: Morning — I'll be honest with you, I'm not sure this call is even the right one to be making, but is there someone who looks after marketing or the website for the business?
script.hook: I build simple one-off websites for smaller local merchants who don't have one yet — but looking at what you've already got here, a proper site, hundreds of reviews, I don't think that's you.
script.valueStatement: Honestly, the sort of thing I do is a fairly small, one-off site for a business that doesn't have one at all. From what I can see you've already got a proper website and a strong online presence, so it probably isn't a fit.
script.demoOffer: I wasn't really expecting to get this far, if I'm honest — you're already well set up online. There isn't really anything I'd suggest building for you.
script.pricing: It's four hundred pounds for the kind of small one-off site I build — but given what you've already got, I don't think that's relevant here.
